name: Ibogaine and noribogaine
short: Deaths: 27 reported by 2016, and a case of cardiac arrest and brain death. Case reports of QT prolongation and ventricular arrhythmias, some in people with no known heart disease.
text: The evidence of serious harm comes from case reports and uncontrolled studies, so, as a 2022 systematic review notes, causation cannot be clearly established. A 2016 review states that 27 fatalities have been reported after ibogaine was taken by mouth; pre-existing heart conditions were implicated in the deaths with post-mortem data, but the review presents 8 case reports suggesting that ibogaine caused ventricular tachyarrhythmias (dangerous fast heart rhythms) and QT-interval prolongation in people without a pre-existing heart condition or family history, and says that noribogaine, its main breakdown product, appears at least as harmful to heart function. A case report describes a 40-year-old man who used ibogaine for heroin withdrawal symptoms and had a cardiac arrest leading to brain swelling and brain death. The 2022 systematic review of 18 studies (2015 to 2020) classed the acute adverse events as mainly cardiac, most commonly QTc prolongation, plus gastrointestinal and neurological effects, and the longer-lasting ones as mainly persistent heart changes and psychiatric and neurological signs. In 14 people with opioid use disorder given a single dose of ibogaine hydrochloride, the authors conclude that QTc prolongation and cerebellar effects (on balance and coordination) are most likely driven by ibogaine rather than noribogaine, and blood levels varied with CYP2D6 genotype; the abstract does not give the size of the QTc change. In contrast, an open-label observational study of 30 male military veterans with mostly mild traumatic brain injury, given ibogaine together with magnesium and other treatments, reported no unexpected or serious adverse events. Interactions: the 2016 review says ibogaine is broken down mainly by the enzyme CYP2D6 to noribogaine, and that polymorphism (variation) in CYP2D6 can influence blood levels of both ibogaine and noribogaine, which may matter when a person takes other medicines that are subject to significant CYP2D6 metabolism; it expects more deaths particularly in people with pre-existing heart conditions and those taking other medicines at the same time.
